chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A woman from our family, her brother died and he bequeathed [the cost of] a Hajj, and the woman had already performed Hajj. She said: 'If I am well, I will perform Hajj on behalf of my brother, and I am more rightful to it than others.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem if she performs Hajj on behalf of her brother; and if she has wealth, let her perform Hajj from her own wealth, for it is greater for her reward.'
ai.seo_question: Can a woman perform Hajj on behalf of her deceased brother using her own money?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the permissibility of a woman performing Hajj on behalf of her deceased brother, resolving the potential conflict with her having already fulfilled her own obligatory Hajj (*Hajj al-Islam*). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes that while the bequest covers the cost, utilizing her personal wealth for this voluntary act (*Hajj al-Nafila*) yields greater spiritual reward, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the merit of self-funded devotion in addition to fulfilling obligations. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding *Hajj al-Nafil* for both genders, provided the prerequisite obligatory Hajj has been completed.
